title: Make a VCF Automation policy upsert safe to deliver twice
prompt:
Our policy reconciler pushes guardrail policies into VMware Cloud Foundation Automation 9.1 (the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation). It runs every ten minutes from a job that gets killed and restarted, and last week a flapping load balancer left us with four copies of the same lease policy, three of them shadowing the one the platform team edits. The upsert has to become something we can deliver twice without getting two policies.

`client.go` is the package that does the pushing. It compiles and every function in it returns "not implemented". Implement it.

`docs/contract.json` is the wire contract, transcribed from the VCF Automation xAPIs reference on developer.broadcom.com; `docs/official_sources.json` records which page each part came from. VCF Automation ships no published specification, so that reference is all there is: the contract says where it is silent and what this repository decided instead. Read it first — it names both operations you may call, the properties each one takes, and which of them the server owns.

What `EnsurePolicy` has to do:

- Choose the policy id once per upsert, before the first delivery, and put it in the request body. That is what makes the call repeatable: the API creates the policy or updates the one at that id. A caller-supplied `PolicySpec.ID` is used as given; otherwise mint one through `Config.NewPolicyID`, which defaults to a random version 4 UUID. Every delivery of one upsert carries the same id and the same bytes.
- Report the outcome from the status: 201 is `OutcomeCreated`, 200 is `OutcomeUpdated`.
- Read the stored policy back and return it in `Result.Policy`.
- Retry a delivery that failed at the transport, and one answered 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504, up to `Config.MaxAttempts` (default 4), waiting `Config.RetryDelay` in between and giving up as soon as the context is done. Every other documented status is terminal — including 202, which names nothing this API lets you poll.
- Tell the two kinds of failure apart. A response with a status is an observed outcome, so a retryable status is delivered again directly. A transport failure is not: the write may have landed and the acknowledgement gone missing. Before delivering again, find out — if the policy is there, that delivery landed, so report `OutcomeRecovered` with the policy you found instead of sending a second one.
- Leave out what was not set. An optional property the caller left empty is absent from the request JSON, not sent as `""`, `null` or `{}`, and a property the contract marks server-owned is never sent at all. A query parameter that is not being requested is absent from the URL rather than set to its default. Send no header the contract does not name for the operation.
- Return an API response failure as `*APIError` carrying the operation, method, path, status and complete response body, and never put the bearer token in an error message. After a policy id has been chosen, a failure result still carries `PolicyID` and the number of delivery `Attempts`, so an operator can reconcile by hand.

Constraints: `client.go` is the only file to change. Go standard library only — no new module dependencies. Leave `go.mod`, `docs/`, `internal/vcfamock/`, `policy_upsert_test.go` and `.gitignore` alone.

`policy_upsert_test.go` is the acceptance test. It runs the loopback service in `internal/vcfamock`, which is pinned to `docs/contract.json` and serves only the operations named there, and it reads that service's request log to check the wire shape of everything you send. No live VMware endpoint is involved.

Acceptance: `go test -race -timeout 120s ./...`

prerequisites.note: gcc is required because the acceptance command runs under -race.

research.interface: VCF Automation API policy upsert - POST /policy/api/policies with GET /policy/api/policies/{id}
research.basis_note: VCF Automation has no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository, so docs/contract.json was transcribed by hand from the rendered VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com. The contract states that plainly and separates what the reference documents from what this repository decided where the reference is silent. The full page-by-page record, including pages surveyed and rejected, is in files/docs/official_sources.json.

official_sources.title: Create Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Policies | VCF Automation API
official_sources.used_for: POST /policy/api/policies, 'Creates a new policy, updates an existing policy, or trigger a policy dry-run.'; the full Policy request body property list with types, formats, required flags and the maxLength 1024 / maxLength 2000 / SOFT|HARD constraints; id typed string format uuid and optional, which is what lets the client choose it; dryRun and validationOnly query parameters; statuses 200/201/202/400/401/403, each 'Operation doesn't return any data structure'; bearerAuth; curl example carrying Authorization and Content-Type only

official_sources.title: Create Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Catalog | VCF Automation API
official_sources.used_for: second portal rendering of the same operation, used to cross-check the property list and status set; it disagreed only on the type of the dryRun query parameter, which is why the contract records that parameter without pinning a type

official_sources.title: Get Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Policies | VCF Automation API
official_sources.used_for: GET /policy/api/policies/{id}; required path parameter id; optional computeStats query parameter; statuses 200/401/403/404; the full Policy response property list including statistics with enforcedCount, notEnforcedCount and conflictCount. This is the only one of the two operations documenting a response body, which is why the stored policy is read back through it

official_sources.title: VCF Automation API Reference Guide Operations Index
official_sources.used_for: confirmed the operation set for a policy upsert, and that request/task resources exist only under /deployment/api - nothing under /policy/api - which is the evidence behind treating a 202 from the upsert as unresolvable

official_sources.title: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Policies
official_sources.used_for: API title 'VCF Automation API', description 'A multi-cloud API for Cloud Automation Services', versions 9.1 (Latest) and 9.0

official_sources.title: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Catalog
official_sources.used_for: corroborated title, description and version listing; documented the OData-like collection query parameters, none of which apply to these two operations

official_sources.title: Request Catalog Item Instances | VM Apps Org - Catalog
official_sources.used_for: surveyed and rejected as the mutating operation: CatalogItemRequest carries no client-choosable identity, so redelivering it creates another deployment

official_sources.title: VCF Automation and All Apps API - Broadcom TechDocs
official_sources.used_for: checked for a versioned media type such as application/json;version=9.1.0; the page names no request header, so none was invented and the contract's header set stays as small as the reference's curl example

research.language_rationale: The reconciler this package belongs to is Go, and retry safety here is a concurrency and wire-shape problem rather than a data-modelling one: the id has to be minted once per upsert and shared by every delivery, the request bytes have to be identical across deliveries, and an unacknowledged delivery has to be told apart from a rejected one. A stdlib net/http implementation exercised by table-driven tests under -race puts all of that under test without a dependency.

scenario: a policy reconciler upserts a VCF Automation policy through POST /policy/api/policies with a client-chosen id, so that a redelivered request converges on one policy, and reads it back through GET /policy/api/policies/{id} because the upsert documents no response body
constraint: the loopback request log proves contract-exact requests, omission of unset optional properties and undocumented headers, one id per upsert reused by every delivery, reconciliation before redelivering an unacknowledged write, and no second policy
